events.headline: Nico Collins out for Week 2 vs. Bengals after missing Thursday and Friday practice
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 17 item. Collins did not practice Thursday or Friday on the Grade 1 hamstring strain he suffered Wednesday, and Houston lists him out for Sunday against Cincinnati. Team doctors have not called the injury serious, so this reads as a one-week absence rather than a longer one, but Jayden Higgins is already gone with a torn ACL, leaving Xavier Hutchinson and Jaylin Noel as the next receivers in line for C.J. Stroud.
events.so_what: Nothing left to hedge: Collins is not in a Week 2 lineup, so start your next-best WR and treat Hutchinson and Noel as thin-bench fliers only. Do not drop Collins for them, since a Grade 1 strain with no IR talk is a one-week hole.

league_notes.hbgbs: Rostered by Stipe.
league_notes.pit: Rostered by YOU (ThatWasButtery) -- start your next-best WR this week.

events.headline: Murray ruled out for Week 2 at Chicago; Wentz starts again
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 16/17 items. The Vikings officially ruled Murray out for Sunday while he remains in the concussion protocol. Coach Kevin O'Connell said Friday the team "fully anticipates" him clearing the protocol early next week, so this looks like one missed game. Carson Wentz, who finished the Week 1 win over Green Bay, starts, with J.J. McCarthy the backup.
events.so_what: A confirmed one-game QB loss, not a season one. In the Pit and Couples Clash this leaves Murray's owner needing a Week 2 stream at the league's thinnest position (Wentz himself is a viable 4-point-TD stream if he is on the wire), and Murray should be back for Week 3.

league_notes.hbgbs: Murray is unrostered in the HBGBs.

events.headline: Kamara cleared: full practice, no designation, set for his 2026 debut vs. Ravens
events.detail: Correction: the earlier version of this item cited a rib injury and a game against Tampa Bay, which was a stale source and is wrong. Kamara was a full participant Friday, carries no game designation on the Saints' Week 2 report and said on Thursday "I'm going," with the Saints expecting his 2026 debut Sunday at Baltimore. He missed the Week 1 game at Detroit.
events.so_what: Kamara's return takes work off Travis Etienne, so the Etienne owner should not assume a full early-down role. Mark Ingram is no longer a pickup case. Kamara is a start wherever he is healthy on your roster, at an RB slot that rewards his receiving work.

events.headline: Flowers doubtful vs. Saints after a limited Friday practice; Bateman leads the WR room
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 16/17 items. Flowers missed Wednesday and Thursday, returned as a limited participant Friday, and is officially doubtful for Sunday against New Orleans with the hamstring injury; reporting says he is not expected to be available. If he sits, Baltimore turns to Rashod Bateman, Chris Moore, Devontez Walker (full practice after missing the opener with a groin injury) and LaJohntay Wester, with rookie Elijah Sarratt a possible debut.
events.so_what: Treat him as out for lineup purposes: doubtful with one limited practice is not a clear-by-Sunday signal. The limited Friday session points to a Week 3 return. Bateman is the receiver to look at first if he is on your wire.

league_notes.hbgbs: Flowers is pauldag's -- the same roster already down A.J. Brown, so WR is now thin there.
league_notes.clash: Flowers is on YOUR roster (ThatWasButtery) -- plan around him being out.

events.headline: Bowers doubtful vs. Chargers after first practice since knee surgery; Mayer likely starts
events.detail: Corrects the earlier Friday note that had him missing a third straight practice: Bowers did practice Friday for the first time since a Sept. 8 meniscus trim, and the Raiders list him doubtful for Sunday at the Chargers. He is expected to test the knee in pregame warmups as a game-time call, but the team is leaning toward holding him out and targeting Week 3 at New Orleans. Michael Mayer, who had six catches for 32 yards in Week 1, starts if he sits.
events.so_what: Plan on Mayer as the Week 2 TE, and do not bench a healthy alternative for Bowers on a warmup rumor. Bowers is a stash, not a Sunday play, with Week 3 the realistic target.

events.headline: Okonkwo out for Week 2 at Dallas with hamstring injury
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 16 item. Washington lists Okonkwo out on the final report for Sunday at Dallas after he missed practice with the hamstring injury suffered late in the Week 1 loss to Philadelphia. John Bates and Ben Sinnott are next in line at tight end.

He is expected to play alongside Rhamondre Stevenson in New England's backfield.

events.headline: Burrow questionable but a full participant Friday, expected to start vs. Texans
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 17 item. Burrow moved from limited practices to full participation Friday on the back tightness, and coach Zac Taylor said he "feels good." The Bengals still list him questionable, with the official call coming at inactives roughly 90 minutes before kickoff. Joe Flacco is the backup.
events.so_what: A full Friday makes him a start, with the tag a formality unless something flares in warmups. Keep a streamer in mind only if your league has no late-game QB swap, since this is the one position with no margin.

events.headline: Olave questionable for Week 2 with a hamstring injury
events.detail: Olave is listed questionable for Sunday at Baltimore with a hamstring injury after a limited practice Thursday, per the Saints' Friday report. He does not carry a doubtful tag, and his status resolves at Sunday inactives.
events.so_what: A real game-time call for a WR1: if he sits, Devaughn Vele (9 targets in Week 1) is the direct beneficiary and an easy start, so owners of both should read the inactives before locking either lineup.

events.headline: Rush set to start again for Falcons as Tua sits out Friday too; Pitts' role shrinks under the backup QB
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 14/16 items. Cooper Rush was a full practice participant again Friday and remains on track to start Sunday against Carolina, while Tagovailoa (oblique) did not practice all week. Under Rush in Week 1, Kyle Pitts played just 39 of 61 snaps and saw one target as the offense funneled attempts to Bijan Robinson (7 of 14 first-half pass attempts); Pitts' outlook is tied to Tagovailoa or Penix getting back on the field.
events.so_what: The QB question stays a wash for Robinson and London's own lineup rather than a run-game change, but it's now a confirmed drag on Pitts specifically -- his already-thin tight end value in this format is capped as long as Rush is throwing it, not just a one-week fluke.

league_notes.hbgbs: Robinson and London are both pauldag's -- the QB uncertainty is a wash for that roster's lineup, not a start/sit call; Rush is unrostered.

events.headline: McConkey takes part in Friday walkthrough, trending toward a questionable Sunday
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 14/16 items. After sitting out practice entirely Wednesday and Thursday on the rib injury, McConkey took part in Friday's walkthrough, per ESPN's Kris Rhim. He carries an official questionable tag for Sunday's game against the Raiders.
events.so_what: Working back in on the final practice day is a real step forward for a game-time-decision watch, but questionable after two full DNPs still isn't a clearance -- worth a bench alternative ready in this 5-bench-spot format rather than pencilling him in before Sunday's inactive list.

league_notes.hbgbs: Rostered by bwalsh89.

events.headline: Allen limited again Friday but expected to suit up Sunday vs. Broncos
events.detail: Updates the Sept. 8/12 items. LeQuint Allen carried a limited tag through Friday's practice on the hip injury that had him as a Week 1 game-time call, but is now expected to play Sunday against Denver alongside Bhayshul Tuten in Jacksonville's shared backfield.
events.so_what: This resolves last week's game-time-decision uncertainty toward Allen actually suiting up, but it doesn't resolve the touch split -- both backs still price as low-end RB2/FLEX plays in this bell-cow-preferring format rather than one clear starter until the workload tilts one way.

events.headline: Darnold ruled out for Week 2 with glute injury -- Drew Lock starts vs. Cardinals
events.detail: Seattle ruled Darnold out for Sunday's game at Arizona with what the team called a unique soft-tissue injury to his glute suffered on a third-down sack in the opener. The Seahawks clarified his hip joint itself isn't affected and have no plans to put him on injured reserve, with a return targeted in a few weeks rather than a lengthy absence. Drew Lock -- who relieved Darnold last week and went 16-of-22 for 187 yards and a touchdown -- gets the start, with Jalen Milroe as his backup.
events.so_what: This is a confirmed multi-week loss at the league's shallowest starting position -- in a 4-point-passing-TD format, Lock is a real streaming option off waivers for a team that needs quality volume there, not just a token fill-in.

league_notes.pit: Darnold is LaPray0814's -- Lock is worth a streaming look on waivers.
league_notes.clash: Darnold is haleymegert's -- Lock is worth a streaming look on waivers.

events.headline: Vikings place Mason on IR with fractured thumb -- Jones now the clear early-down back
events.detail: Minnesota placed Jordan Mason on injured reserve Wednesday for a fractured thumb that already required a surgical procedure, ruling him out at least four games (the Vikings' Week 6 bye pushes his earliest eligible return to Week 7). Aaron Jones, who split early-down work with Mason in Week 1 (12 carries, 40 yards, a touchdown), now takes over as the clear lead back. Minnesota signed DeeJay Dallas off the practice squad for depth.
events.so_what: This resolves last week's backfield timeshare question in this bell-cow-preferring format's favor -- Jones is now a confident every-down start for at least a month, not a hedge against a committee partner.

league_notes.hbgbs: Jones is StoneBone69's -- a clean workhorse role now for at least four games. Mason was on DiaperDutyDaddy's bench, a real IR-stash decision.

events.headline: Devaughn Vele looks like a real Saints WR2 with Jordyn Tyson out roughly two months
events.detail: Vele caught 7 of 9 targets for 69 yards and a touchdown in New Orleans' overtime loss to Detroit, stepping into the No. 2 receiver role behind Chris Olave while rookie Jordyn Tyson is out. Tyson left Thursday's practice before the opener with a hamstring injury and, after consulting multiple doctors over the weekend, is now expected to miss roughly two months rather than the four-game minimum first reported.
events.so_what: A 9-target workload in a pass-heavy offense is a real, immediate role rather than a wait-and-see committee note -- worth rostering now in any league where he's still available, and worth planning around a two-month absence for Tyson rather than a four-game one.

league_notes.hbgbs: Vele is bwalsh89's -- a real Week 2 role now, not a speculative add.

events.headline: Stribling's IR timeline lengthens to about 10 weeks after ankle surgery -- Demarcus Robinson still the 49ers' WR3
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 14/16 item. Stribling underwent surgery Wednesday for the deltoid ankle sprain and is now expected to miss close to 10 weeks, a longer absence than the four-game IR minimum first reported. Coach Kyle Shanahan said the hope is he returns later this season. Demarcus Robinson, who had 2 catches for 50 yards and a touchdown in the Week 1 opener, remains the 49ers' WR3 behind Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel while Stribling is out.
events.so_what: Ten weeks is a season-altering absence rather than a short IR stash -- expect the extra volume this format rewards to keep funneling to Evans and Samuel for roughly half the season, with Robinson the deeper-bench name worth knowing if either starter needs a rest day.

league_notes.hbgbs: Evans is StoneBone69's, Samuel is ENOTS's; Stribling and Robinson are both unrostered league-wide.

events.headline: Browns' Sampson placed on IR, out a minimum of four games -- earliest return Week 6
events.detail: Updates the Sept. 14 item. Cleveland placed Sampson on injured reserve Tuesday for the knee injury that knocked him out early in Sunday's loss at Jacksonville, one of eight roster moves announced that day. The IR designation locks in a minimum four-game absence, with Week 6 at home against Baltimore his earliest eligible return. Raheim Sanders, who opened the season as Cleveland's No. 3 back, remains next in line for touches behind starter Quinshon Judkins.
events.so_what: This is now a confirmed month-long bench-spot loss in a 5-bench-spot format rather than a wait-and-see situation -- Judkins remains the clear early-down starter, unaffected, but Sanders is a real handcuff to know for the next several weeks if anything happens to him.

events.headline: Panthers' Jalen Coker breaks out with 138 yards, 2 TDs on 8/9 targets, leads team in snaps
events.detail: Coker caught 8 of his 9 targets for a career-high 138 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 59-37 loss to the Bears, leading Carolina in both snaps (57, 84% of the offense) and routes run (40) with a 26.5% target share. He played through a first-quarter ankle roll -- wearing a walking boot postgame as a precaution -- but said Monday he doesn't expect it to cost him any time and expects to practice this week ahead of Week 2 at Atlanta.
events.so_what: An 84%-snap, 26%-target-share role in this format's 2-FLEX lineup shape is a clear starting-caliber workload rather than a one-game fluke -- worth adding now in a league where he's unrostered rather than waiting on a second game to confirm it.

league_notes.hbgbs: Rostered by StoneBone69.

events.headline: Kenneth Walker III bell-cows Chiefs debut with 173 rush yards, 2 total TDs; Pacheco now buried on Lions' IR
events.detail: Walker, who left Seattle in free agency for a three-year, $43.05M deal after winning Super Bowl MVP there, carried 23 times for 173 yards and a touchdown and added 3 catches for 18 yards and a receiving score in Monday night's 31-10 win over Denver -- the most rushing yards by a Chiefs back since Jamaal Charles in 2012. Isiah Pacheco, who Kansas City could have re-signed, chose Detroit instead once Walker's deal was done; he opened the season on the Lions' injured reserve and didn't play Week 1. Emmett Johnson and Brashard Smith are the backups behind Walker in Kansas City's backfield.
events.so_what: This format's bell-cow-preferring scoring got exactly the outcome it wants here -- Walker looks like a clear, three-down workload back rather than part of a timeshare, which is the archetype this league's roster construction rewards most.

league_notes.hbgbs: Walker is Sladsous's.

events.headline: 49ers rookie Black matched McCaffrey's touch count in Week 1 -- an early committee signal to track
events.detail: Rookie Kaelon Black played 28 snaps (36% of routes run) to McCaffrey's 35 snaps (56% of routes) in San Francisco's Week 1 win over the Rams, and out-carried him 14-10 while finishing with an identical 15 total touches. McCaffrey still handled the passing-down and red-zone work. Coach Kyle Shanahan hasn't announced a formal plan for how the workload splits going forward.
events.so_what: A rookie already earning a near-even carry split behind the starter is worth tracking early -- McCaffrey still holds the passing-down role that a bell-cow-preferring format like this one prices highest, but a second straight week of a 14-carry rookie would be a real value shift rather than a one-game fluke.

events.headline: Jaguars' Thomas expected to play Week 2 after early exit with shoulder injury
events.detail: Thomas left Sunday's blowout win over Cleveland in the second quarter with a shoulder injury but returned for Jacksonville's final drive of the first half, an encouraging sign. Coach Liam Coen said Monday he expects Thomas to play in Week 2 against Denver, likely with a limited practice week and instructions to avoid unnecessary contact rather than a hard snap-count plan.
events.so_what: A limited-practice, expected-to-play designation with no setback reported is a lean-start signal rather than a bench call in this format's WR math -- worth a final look at Friday's official tag, but the early read favors starting him over a bench alternative.

league_notes.hbgbs: Rostered by Sladsous.

events.headline: Brown's IR timeline lengthens to six weeks, not four — earliest return is Week 8
events.detail: Updates the Sept. 11 item. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport now reports Brown is expected to miss roughly six weeks with the high-ankle sprain, not the four-game minimum first reported when he landed on IR. He'll avoid surgery. Six weeks pushes his earliest eligible return to Week 6 (he's IR-eligible to activate then) with Week 8 vs. Miami the more realistic target — two weeks longer than the original CBS Sports report, and it now spans the Steelers, Jaguars, Bills, Raiders, Jets and Bears games.
events.so_what: Two extra weeks out is a bigger bench-spot commitment in a league with only 5 bench spots — Brown's own roster should stop treating this as a short-term IR stash and plan the next six weeks around Doubs and Williams rather than counting down to an October return.

league_notes.hbgbs: Brown is rostered by pauldag, who needs to fill this spot from waivers now rather than just riding out a bye. Doubs is on mfkr's roster; Williams is unrostered league-wide. events.headline: Love active vs. Chargers and scores a TD, but Allgeier out-touches him 19-13 in Cardinals' backfield
events.detail: Updates the Sept. 11 item. Love was cleared and played Sunday against the Chargers, rushing 11 times for 41 yards and a 5-yard touchdown while adding 2 catches for 9 yards -- but Tyler Allgeier out-snapped him 44-32 and out-touched him 19-13 in Arizona's 26-14 win. Love forced six missed tackles and gained 38 of his 41 yards after contact.
events.so_what: Cleared to play removes the injury variable, but the touch count says this opens as a real committee rather than a bell-cow breakout for either back -- Love's per-touch efficiency is a name worth watching, but neither back is a confident starter over a bench alternative in this format until the touch split tilts clearly one way.

league_notes.hbgbs: Love is mfkr's, Allgeier is ENOTS's -- a committee split across two different rosters, not one.
